- MAP that ties milestones to commercial terms (we need pricing triggers for commit size)
- Suggested GPU pool sizing for a pilot (~1–2 wks of eval) and a production ramp plan
- Any burst clauses or overage terms for Q1 usage spikes

Can you send a draft MAP and an initial sizing recommendation? Timelines: Priya is aiming to have procurement engaged by next Wednesday (6/30).

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood demo follow-up — next steps for eval & capacity

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick follow. Attaching a draft MAP (MAP_Finera_v1.pdf) and a short GPU sizing worksheet (GPU_Sizing_Worksheet.xlsx) so your infra and procurement teams can review. Summary below — happy to iterate: 

Overview (proposal):
- 2-week evaluation sprint (non-binding): 2x A100-equivalent GPUs dedicated to your tenant in our sandbox region for throughput and latency validation. Objective: validate 95th percentile inference latency and token/sec under your prompt mix.
- Pilot commitment (90 days): reserve 4 GPUs (baseline) dedicated; included burst window (see below). Pricing discount: 10% off list for the 90-day pilot if pilot success criteria met.
- Production ramp (12-month term): scale to 10 GPUs (committed) with tiered discounts: 12-month term — 18% off list at commit >=10 GPUs; 24-month term — 25% off list at commit >=10 GPUs.

MAP milestones (proposed dates tied to procurement):
1) Week 0–2 (evaluation sprint) — acceptance criteria: throughput >= target, no >2s tail latency on majority of prompts. Passing this triggers the pilot pricing offer. Target completion: 2026-07-10.
2) Week 3–6 (pilot + integration) — pilot success review and sign-off; hardware reservation requested by 2026-07-24.
3) Week 7–12 (production roll) — final capacity ramp and billing transition; contract signature to take effect on start date.

Burst & overage terms (short summary):
- Burst headroom: customer may exceed committed pool up to 2x provisioned GPUs for up to 30 cumulative days per rolling quarter. Burst usage billed at 1.5x of list rate above committed baseline.
- Emergency burst (temporary, <72 hours) can be accommodated at no surcharge if capacity available and approved by Redwood SRE.

Attachments: MAP_Finera_v1.pdf (draft MAP with milestone checkboxes), GPU_Sizing_Worksheet.xlsx (worksheet with expected vCPU/RAM/IO and model footprints).

Next steps: 
- Can you confirm who on procurement/legal should be included?
- If acceptable, Marissa will finalize pricing sheet and we can lock in pilot pricing by COB Mon 6/29.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Draft MAP & eval sprint — notes on pricing cadence

Grace — quick internal notes (looping Karthik):

- Proposed pilot discount 10% looks fine. For the production tiering, suggest we make the 12-month 18% a "standard" offer and reserve 24-month 25% for pursuit approval (deal desk).
- For burst clause, recommend capping emergency free bursts to 48 hours (not 72) unless SRE explicitly approves longer. Also propose adding a per-quarter burst cap of 30 days total (matches customer-facing doc).
- Add a clause: if customer exceeds 3x committed baseline for more than 7 consecutive days, we trigger a capacity review and may require a temporary capacity purchase at full list.

Marissa to own pricing sheet update and send a formal quote draft. Karthik — can you confirm GPU availability in us-west-2 for July 10 pilot start?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Account Execs, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Alex
